items.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued July 13 at 4:44PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
ESFAFC

* Glacier Creek in Girdwood

* Early Tuesday morning through Noon Wednesday

Rainfall:

* Around 1.5 inches of rain is expected Monday evening through
Wednesday morning in the Chugach Mountains draining into Glacier
Creek.

Hydrologic Concerns:

* Bankfull conditions can cause water to cover the lowest sections of
Lake Tahoe Road.

* Heavy rain may result in localized ponding in low-lying areas and
locations with poor drainage.

items.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued July 13 at 4:18PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
ESFAFC

* Yentna and Skwentna River drainages

* Monday night through Saturday morning

Rainfall:

* Widespread rainfall of 1.5 to 2.5 inches of rain is expected in
the western Susitna Valley through Wednesday.

Hydrologic Concerns:

* Expect sharp rises on many small streams and rivers. Crests are
expected to occur on Wednesday for most streams and rivers.

* Many lower locations along rivers such as gravel bars and other
spots popular for camping and recreating may become inundated with
water

items.headline: Wind Advisory issued July 13 at 3:23PM AKDT until July 14 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Southeast winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts of 45 to 65 mph
expected.

* WHERE...South Anchorage, the Anchorage Hillside and Turnagain Arm.

* WHEN...From 4 AM to 10 PM AKDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects and a few
power outages may result. Winds this strong can make driving
difficult, especially for high profile vehicles.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds will increase along the Hillside and
Turnagain Arm tonight with strong winds moving into Anchorage

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 13 at 2:15PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
Rain is expected everyday through the week with periods of heavy
rain likely at times, especially along the southern slopes of the
Eastern Alaska Range on Tuesday and Wednesday. From Monday
afternoon through Thursday morning, rainfall totals will be around
1 to 3 inches with locally higher amounts in the summits above
5000 feet. South winds will also be gusty, up to 45 mph which can
result in localized tree damage. However, wind gusts of 65 to 75
mph will reside just to the north.
items.areas: Southern Denali Borough; Eastern Alaska Range South of Trims Camp

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 13 at 2:11PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
Weak south to southwesterly wind will result in minor sea level
rises. Expect rises of 1 to 3 feet above the normal high tide
line with each high tide cycle through Tuesday. Winds will be
weakening and shifting northerly on Tuesday.

The highest water levels, up to 3 feet above the high tide line,
are expected in Eastern Norton Sound while the Yukon Delta and
Nome Coast are expected to be around 1 to 2 feet.
